rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari accepts the grammatical analysis but finds it semantically weak: moderation between extravagance and miserliness is self-evidently balanced, so the report adds nothing.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وهو من جهة الإعراب لا بأس به، ولكن المعنى ليس بقوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse praises measured spending between excess and shortfall, as the Prophet was likewise told not to keep his hand chained or extend it fully.
rows.anchor: وصفهم تعالى بالقصد الذي هو بين الغلو والتقصير، وبمثله خوطب الرسول

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports asking the Prophet the gravest sin: associating a partner with God, killing one's child from fear of sharing food, then adultery with a neighbor's wife; the verse confirmed this ranking.
rows.anchor: سأل ابن مسعود رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أي الذنب أعظم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another occasion report says idolaters who had committed many murders and adulteries asked whether their past acts had expiation; the passage through Forgiving, Merciful was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أتي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مشركون قد قتلوا فأكثروا وزنوا فأكثروا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further report connects the revelation to Wahshi's conversion, in a lengthy account.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزولها قصة وحشي في إسلامه في حديث طويل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the denial of grave sins among the believers' virtues as an implicit exposure of Quraysh and other enemies, whom God left in their own corrupt conduct.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: نفى هذه التقبيحات العظام عن الموصوفين بتلك الخلال العظيمة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the passage distinguishes believers from unbelievers' idolatry, female infanticide, injustice, raiding, and zina, which they treated as permissible.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: إخراج لعباده المؤمنين من صفات الكفرة في عبادتهم الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on killing a protected soul has a parallel already interpreted in Surat al-Anam.
rows.anchor: وتقدم تفسير نظير ولا تقتلوا النفس التي حرم الله إلا بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is read yulaqqā with passive formation and doubled qaf; Ibn Masud and Abu Raja read yulqā with an alif, retaining the alif despite its implied case ending.
rows.anchor: وقرئ يلق بضم الياء وفتح اللام والقاف مشددة وابن مسعود وأبو رجاء يلقى بألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athām lexically means punishment, the recompense for sin; the cited verse of poetry uses it for a penalty or legal punishment.
rows.anchor: والأثام في اللغة العقاب وهو جزاء الإثم. قال الشاعر:

rows.speaker: قتادة وزيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Qatada and Zayd ibn Aslam explain athām as a legal penalty and punishment.
rows.anchor: وبه فسره قتادة وابن زيد

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو ومجاهد وعكرمة وابن جبير
rows.claim: They interpret Athām as a valley in Hell bearing that name, made by God as punishment for unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو ومجاهد وعكرمة وابن جبير: أثام واد في جهنم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim takes athām to mean sin itself, with the wording naming the sin for its recompense.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: الأثام الإثم، ومعناه يلق جزاء أثام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says Athām is one of the names of Hell; other views identify it as a well or a mountain.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: الأثام اسم من أسماء جهنم. وقيل: بئر فيها. وقيل: جبل.

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud's reading ayyāman, plural of day, means severe ordeals, as in calling a harsh day a day of days.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: يلق أياما جمع يوم يعني شدائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase points to the combined acts of idolatry, unlawful killing, and adultery; doubled punishment attaches to the aggregate and need not attach to each offense separately, while unbelievers' punishment varies by crime.
rows.anchor: ومن يفعل ذلك يظهر أنه إشارة إلى المجموع من دعاء إله وقتل النفس بغير حق والزنا

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers use passive yudāʿaf with an alif, followed by active yukhlad.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي يضاعف له العذاب مبنيا للمفعول وبألف ويخلد مبنيا للفاعل

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو جعفر وابن كثير
rows.claim: They keep the same voice pattern as the preceding reading but double the ʿayn and omit the alif.
rows.anchor: والحسن وأبو جعفر وابن كثير كذلك إلا أنهم شددوا العين وطرحوا الألف

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة وطلحة بن سليمان
rows.claim: Their variant has first-person plural passive nudaʿʿif, with al-ʿadhāb as an accusative object.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر أيضا وشيبة وطلحة بن سليمان نضعف بالنون مضمومة وكسر العين مشددة العذاب نصب

rows.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
rows.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif reads active yudāʿifu and puts al-ʿadhāb in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وطلحة بن مصرف يضاعف بالياء مبنيا للفاعل العذاب نصبا

rows.speaker: طلحة بن سليمان
rows.claim: Talha ibn Sulayman reads tukhlad with second-person address as an apostrophe to the unbeliever.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة بن سليمان وتخلد بتاء الخطاب على الالتفات مرفوعا

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Haywa reads passive, doubled yukhlad in the jussive; the light form is also related from Abu Amr.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة ويخلد مبنيا للمفعول مشدد اللام مجزوما

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم وابن عامر والمفضل عن عاصم والأعمش
rows.claim: Further readings raise both verbs; the cited transmissions include passive forms, both light and doubled, with the al-Aʿmash form doubled.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم يضاعف ويخلد بالرفع عنهما وكذا ابن عامر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The raised forms are understood as a new sentence or circumstantial clause, whereas the jussive is an appositional substitute for yلق.
rows.anchor: فالرفع على الاستئناف أو الحال والجزم على البدل من يلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line exemplifies the construction in which the jussive follows the conditional verb.
rows.anchor: متى تأتنا تلمم بنا في ديارنا ... تجد حطبا جزلا ونارا تأججا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in fīhi refers to the punishment.
rows.anchor: والضمير في فيه عائد على العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's position is that a Muslim who committed unlawful murder can repent successfully, contrary to Ibn Abbas; he notes the earlier discussion in Surat al-Nisa.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن توبة المسلم القاتل النفس بغير حق مقبولة خلافا لابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains replacing sins with good deeds as exchanging prior acts of disobedience for obedience, which then becomes a cause of God's mercy.
rows.anchor: تبديل سيئاتهم حسنات هو جعل أعمالهم بدل معاصيهم الأول طاعة ويكون ذلك سبب رحمة الله

rows.speaker: ابن جبير والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: They reject the view that the replacement of bad deeds occurs on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وابن جبير والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد وردوا على من قال هو في يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says a sin itself does not become a good deed: repentance erases it and a good deed is recorded for repentance, while unbelievers' deeds are annulled and sins remain.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: السيئة بعينها لا تصير حسنة، ولكن السيئة تمحى بالتوبة

rows.speaker: ابن مسيب ومكحول
rows.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib and Makhul place the transformation on Judgment Day and understand it as generous forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وتأول ابن مسيب ومكحول أن ذلك يوم القيامة وهو بمعنى كرم العفو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report in Sahih Muslim says God replaces sins with good deeds on the Resurrection Day for monotheists whom He chooses to forgive.
rows.anchor: وفي كتاب مسلم إن الله يبدل يوم القيامة لمن يريد المغفرة له من الموحدين بدل سيئات حسنات

rows.speaker: القفال والقاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal and al-Qadi explain the replacement as changing punishment into reward, naming the consequences by the deeds that cause them.
rows.anchor: وقال القفال والقاضي: يبدل العقاب بالثواب فذكرهما وأراد ما يستحق بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects a connected exception because it would only remove multiplied punishment; he prefers a detached exception: the repentant believer does not suffer punishment, and God replaces sins with good deeds.
rows.anchor: فالأولى عندي أن يكون استثناء منقطعا أي لكن من تاب وآمن عمل صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the replacement clause, their sins are the second object, originally preceded by a preposition, while good deeds are the first, unrestricted object.
rows.anchor: وسيئاتهم هو المفعول الثاني، وهو أصله أن يكون مقيدا بحرف الجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites a parallel phrasing and a line of poetry to illustrate replacing one thing with another.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى وبدلناهم بجنتيهم جنتين . وقال الشاعر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is that whoever undertakes repentance returns to God's reward and beneficence.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن ومن تاب أي أنشأ التوبة فإنه يتوب إلى الله أي يرجع إلى ثوابه وإحسانه

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya reads the clause as praise of the repentant: he has held to a firm matter and will find relief and great forgiveness.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية ومن تاب فإنه قد تمسك بأمر وثيق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari defines repentance as abandoning sins with regret and entering righteous action, trusting God to recognize and reward the rights of those who repent.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ومن يترك المعاصي ويندم عليها ويدخل في العمل الصالح فإنه بذلك تائب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view urges anyone resolved to repent to hurry and turn toward God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من عزم على التوبة فإنه يتوب إلى الله فليبادر إليها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the one who repents returns to the One who accepts repentance and pardons sins.
rows.anchor: وقيل من تاب من ذنوبه فإنه يتوب إلى من يقبل التوبة عن عباده

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view understands the true penitent as someone who remains steadfast in repentance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ومن تاب استقام على التوبة فإنه يتوب إلى الله

rows.speaker: author وعلي والباقر
rows.claim: The apparent interpretation of witnessing no falsehood is not giving false testimony, as Ali and al-Baqir explain it.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن المعنى لا يشهدون بالزور أو شهادة الزور، قاله علي والباقر

rows.speaker: الضحاك وزيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: They identify al-zūr with polytheism and idols.
rows.anchor: فالشرك قاله الضحاك وابن زيد

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن جريج
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies al-zūr as singing, while Ibn Jurayj takes it as lying.
rows.anchor: والغناء قاله مجاهد، والكذب قاله ابن جريج

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن الحنفية ومجاهد
rows.claim: Reports in al-Kashshaf identify it as assemblies of falsehood, amusement and singing, or the festivals of polytheists.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشاف عن قتادة مجالس الباطل. وعن ابن الحنفية: اللهو والغناء. وعن مجاهد: أعياد المشركين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other reported possibilities are musical instruments, Christian holidays, a pre-Islamic game, wailing, or gatherings that disparage the righteous.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى لا يحضرون من المشاهدة والزور الشرك والصنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-laghw encompasses anything that ought to be discarded; the believers pass its people by with dignity, turning away rather than stopping to join their talk.
rows.anchor: وباللغو كل ما ينبغي أن يلغى ويطرح. والمعنى وإذا مروا بأهل اللغو مروا معرضين عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs of their Lord are the Quran.
rows.anchor: بآيات ربهم هي القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negation falls on the qualifiers deaf and blind, not on falling: believers avidly listen and attend, unlike hypocrites who only appear attentive without understanding or insight.
rows.anchor: النفي متوجه إلى القيد الذي هو صم وعميان لا للخرور الداخل عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya instead pictures their falling as prostration and weeping, and construes a falling away as disorderly collapse rather than ordered prostration.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: بل يكون خرورهم سجدا وبكيا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi takes deaf and blind as a description of unbelievers' deliberate rejection; such participial phrases can color an action without asserting the literal posture.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي لم يخروا صما وعميانا هي صفة للكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurrat aʿyun is a metaphor for happiness, associated with cool tears of joy in contrast to hot tears of grief; Abu Tammam's verse and idioms illustrate it.
rows.anchor: قرة أعين كناية عن السرور والفرح، وهو مأخوذ من القر وهو البرد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative derives the phrase from qarār: the gaze settles on the beloved and does not turn elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مأخوذ من القرار أي يقر النظر به ولا ينظر إلى غيره

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr says the coolness of the eye means sleep, because security comes only when fear is absent; al-Qaffal transmits this.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: وقرة العين النوم أي آمنا لأن الأمن لا يأتي مع الخوف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وحضرمي
rows.claim: They explain the joy as seeing spouses and children obedient to God; in early Islam family members could differ in faith, so conversion of loved ones brought joy.
rows.anchor: وقرة العين فيمن ذكروا رؤيتهم مطيعين لله قاله ابن عباس والحسن وحضرمي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also describes a child's joy as seeing him write and study jurisprudence.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: قرة عين الولدان تراه يكتب الفقه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The prayer may seek immediate worldly joy through righteous family members, or ask that those loved ones be joined to the petitioners in Paradise.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنهم دعوا بذلك ليجابوا في الدنيا فيسروا بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request that family be joined in Paradise includes, rather than excludes, the first view about worldly faith, which produces that later joy.
rows.anchor: ويتضمن هذا القول الأول الذي هو في الدنيا لأن ذلك نتيجة إيمانهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition min may mark the starting point or source of joy from spouses and offspring.
rows.anchor: ومن الظاهر أنها لابتداء الغاية أي هب لنا من جهتهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari proposes explanatory min, as if the requested joy were then identified as coming from spouses and descendants; the author objects that min of explanation should follow what it explains and says this use is not established.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن تكون للبيان قاله الزمخشري

rows.speaker: ابن عامر والحرميان وحفص
rows.claim: These readers use the plural dhurriyyātinā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر والحرميان وحفص وذرياتنا على الجمع

rows.speaker: باقي السبعة وطلحة
rows.claim: The remaining canonical readers and Talha use the singular form of dhurriyyatinā.
rows.anchor: وباقي السبعة وطلحة على الإفراد

rows.speaker: عبد الله وأبو الدرداء وأبو هريرة
rows.claim: They read qurrāt in the plural, while the general reading is singular qurrat.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وأبو الدرداء وأبو هريرة قرات على الجمع

rows.speaker: author والزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says indefiniteness conveys joy for a few eyes compared with the many of others; the author rejects the inference because believers' eyes remain numerous, well beyond counting.
rows.anchor: وليس بجيد لأن أعين تنطلق على العشرة فما دونه من الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular imam may stand for a plural, be a cadence-friendly generic, mean each individual an imam, denote a collective, or express unity and agreement.
rows.anchor: وأفرد إماما إما اكتفاء بالواحد عن الجمع، وحسنه كونه فاصلة

rows.speaker: النخعي
rows.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi says the worshippers ask to be religious exemplars, not political rulers; another view says the verse shows religious leadership should be sought, and a report places it among the ten promised Paradise.
rows.anchor: قالوا: واجعلنا إماما واحدا دعوا الله أن يكونوا قدوة في الدين ولم يطلبوا الرئاسة

rows.speaker: author وابن عباس
rows.claim: Those points back to the people described by the ten qualities; al-ghurfa is generic for the chambers, the elevated rooms. Ibn Abbas describes them as houses of emerald, pearl, and ruby.
rows.anchor: أولئك إشارة إلى الموصوفين بهذه الصفات العشرة. والغرفة اسم معرف بأل فيعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Continuing Ibn Abbas description from the preceding segment, the chambers are houses made of emerald, pearl, and ruby.
rows.anchor: وهي بيوت من زبرجد ودر وياقوت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other explanations identify al-ghurfa as a name for Paradise, the seventh heaven, the highest stations in Paradise, or exalted rank.
rows.anchor: وقيل الغرفة من أسماء الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in bimā ṣabarū is causal; alternatively it marks exchange, as the cited poetry illustrates. Patience is left unrestricted to encompass every kind.
rows.anchor: والباء في بما صبروا للسبب. وقيل: للبدل أي بدل صبرهم

rows.speaker: الحسن وشيبة وأبو جعفر والحرميان وأبو عمرو وأبو بكر
rows.claim: These readers pronounce yulaqqawna with passive yāʾ, a fatḥa, and doubled qāf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وشيبة وأبو جعفر والحرميان وأبو عمرو وأبو بكر ويلقون بضم الياء وفتح اللام والقاف مشددة

rows.speaker: طلحة ومحمد اليماني وباقي السبعة
rows.claim: They read yalaqawna with a fatḥa on yāʾ, a still lām, and an undoubled qāf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة ومحمد اليماني وباقي السبعة بفتح الياء وسكون اللام وتخفيف القاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A greeting is a prayer for long life and peace a prayer for safety; angels may greet them, or they may greet one another, and another view treats the greetings as gifts combining benefit and honor.
rows.anchor: والتحية دعاء بالتعمير والسلام دعاء بالسلامة، أي تحييهم الملائكة أو يحيي بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favorable resting place and station deliberately answer the earlier description of Hell as an evil resting place and station.
rows.anchor: حسنت مستقرا ومقاما معادل لقوله في جهنم ساءت مستقرا ومقاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the servants' good deeds and rewards, God orders the Messenger to tell people that their standing before God depends on worship and supplication.
rows.anchor: أمر رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يصرح للناس بأن لا اكتراث لهم عند ربهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supplication may denote worship and calls for help in hardship; grammatically it may be a negative statement or rhetorical question, and the verbal noun may attach to worshippers or to God calling people to obey.
rows.anchor: ودعاؤكم مصدر أضيف إلى الفاعل أي لولا عبادتكم إياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported alternative makes supplication the object of Gods call to people to obey Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أضيف إلى المفعول أي لولا دعاؤه إياكم إلى طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers addressing Quraysh: God cares for them because they beseech Him in hardship, despite their claim that they worship as instructed.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر أن قوله قل ما يعبؤا بكم خطاب لكفار قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial of the Messenger message makes punishment deserved; the punishment results from denial and sawfa delays its arrival.
rows.anchor: فقد كذبتم بما جاء به الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، فتستحقون العقاب

rows.speaker: عبد الله وابن عباس وابن الزبير
rows.claim: They read the wording as al-kāfirūn have denied; the author treats this as an explanatory reading, not Quranic text.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وابن عباس وابن الزبير: فقد كذب الكافرون وهو محمول على أنه تفسير لا قرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most authorities identify lizām as the Battle of Badr, including Ibn Masud and Ubayy.
rows.anchor: والأكثرون على أن اللزام هنا هو يوم بدر وهو قول ابن مسعود وأبي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other interpretations identify the inevitable consequence as punishment in the afterlife, or death specifically as killing at Badr.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عذاب الآخرة. وقيل: الموت ولا يحمل على الموت المعتاد بل القتل ببدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers leaving the threatened subject unspoken: its context is known, while the extent of the threat cannot be fully described. A reading makes the punishment explicit.
rows.anchor: والوجه أن يترك اسم كان غير منطوق به بعد ما علم أنه مما توعد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reader who supplies the omitted subject explicitly reads that the punishment will be inevitable.
rows.anchor: وقد صرح به من قرأ فسوف يكون العذاب لزاما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: As al-Zahrawi transmits it, Ibn Abbas says their denial itself will cling to them and they will receive no repentance.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس فسوف يكون هو أي التكذيب لزاما أي لازما لكم لا تعطون توبة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the address is universal: worshippers and deniers exist among humanity; deniers face the consequence of violating Gods stated rule, like a king warning a disobedient subject.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: والخطاب إلى الناس على الإطلاق ومنهم مؤمنون عابدون

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj reads the future verb with feminine agreement, taking its subject as the outcome.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن جريج: فسوف تكون بتاء التأنيث أي فسوف تكون العاقبة

rows.speaker: الجمهور والمنهال وأبان بن ثعلب وأبو السماك
rows.claim: Most read lizāman with kasra; al-Minhal, Aban ibn Thaʿlab, and Abu al-Sammak use fatḥa as a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور لزاما بكسر اللام. وقرأ المنهال وأبان بن ثعلب وأبو السماك بفتحها

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda cites a poem as evidence for the kasra reading of lizām.
rows.anchor: وأنشد أبو عبيدة على كسر اللام لصخر الغي

rows.speaker: ابن خالويه وأبو السماك
rows.claim: Ibn Khalawayh transmits Abu al-Sammak form lizām on the pattern of ḥudhām, treated as an indeclinable source form.
rows.anchor: ونقل ابن خالويه عن أبي السماك أنه قرأ لزام على وزن حذام

none: Quranic verse text only; no commentary.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya and others say the entire surah is Meccan without disagreement; al-Zamakhshari excepts the passage beginning Subḥān Allāh.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مكية، قال ابن عطية وغيره، بلا خلاف. وقال الزمخشري: إلا قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Khosrow sent a Persian force under a commander whose name is disputed; it defeated the Romans, killed and devastated, and cut their olives. The battle site is variously Adhriʿat and Bosra, the Jazira, or Jordan and Palestine.
rows.anchor: أن كسرى بعث جيشا إلى الروم، وأمر عليهم رجلا، واختلف النقلة في اسمه

rows.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
rows.claim: Mujahid locates the battle in the Jazira; al-Suddi places it in Jordan and Palestine. Muslims grieved because Romans were People of the Book, while Quraysh rejoiced with the Magian Persians.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: التقت بالجزيرة. وقال السدي: بأرض الأردن وفلسطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet predicted Roman victory within a few years; Abu Bakr publicly proclaimed the opening verses and accepted a pre-prohibition wager with Quraysh, later raised to one hundred camels and nine years at the Prophet's direction.
rows.anchor: وأخبر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، أن الروم سيغلبون في بضع سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Romans prevailed in year seven; Ubayy ibn Khalaf was the opposing bettor, with Abd al-Rahman as guarantor. Ubayy later died from a wound inflicted by the Prophet, and another account dates the victory to Hudaybiyya.
rows.anchor: فظهرت الروم على فارس في السنة السابعة، وكان ممن راهن أبي بن خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account places victory for both sides at Badr: Abu Bakr collected the stake from Ubayy's heirs, and the Prophet told him to give it in charity.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان النصر يوم بدر للفريقين، فأخذ أبو بكر الخطر من ذرية أبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A political account says Khosrow ordered Shahrirazan to kill Farrukhan, then appointed Farrukhan and told him to kill his brother; Shahrirazan showed earlier death orders, after which the brothers allied with Caesar and defeated Khosrow.
rows.anchor: فرد الملك إلى أخيه. وكتب شهريزان إلى قيصر ملك الروم، فتعاونا على كسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Roman victory and ensuing Muslim joy are presented as clear signs of prophethood and the Quran's divine origin, since they disclose unseen events.
rows.anchor: وجاء الخبر، ففرح المسلمون. وكان ذلك من الآيات البينات الشاهدة بصحة النبوة

rows.speaker: علي وأبو سعيد الخدري وابن عباس وابن عمر ومعاوية بن قرة والحسن
rows.claim: These authorities read ghulibat as active, with sayughlabun passive; most readers reverse the voices, reading the first passive and the second active.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي، وأبو سعيد الخدري، وابن عباس، وابن عمر، ومعاوية بن قرة، والحسن: غلبت الروم: مبنيا للفاعل

rows.speaker: ابن عمران وعثمان
rows.claim: Ibn Imran and a report from Uthman interpret the active reading as Rome having defeated the Persian side in the nearest Syrian countryside.
rows.anchor: وتأويل ذلك على ما فسره ابن عمران: الروم غلبت على أدنى ريف الشأم

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: Abu Hatim says Rome had prevailed at Badr, distressing Quraysh and delighting believers, and was promised a further victory within a few years.
rows.anchor: وتأوله أبو حاتم على أن الروم غلبت يوم بدر

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers the passive reading ghulibat; he says sayughlabun is generally read active, though the author corrects his claim of unanimity by noting other readers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: والقراءة بضم الغين أصح. وأجمع الناس على سيغلبون بفتح الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author corrects Ibn Atiyya's claim of consensus: readers who use active ghulibat also read the second verb with passive ya, and Ibn Umar is not alone in that reading.
rows.anchor: وقوله: وأجمعوا، ليس كذلك. ألا ترى أن الذين قرأوا غلبت بفتح الغين

rows.speaker: علي وابن عمر ومعاوية بن قرة
rows.claim: They read ghalabihim with a still lām, while the majority read the lām open; a قياس form on the pattern kitāb is also noted for Ibn Umar.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: غلبهم، بفتح الغين واللام: وعلي، وابن عمر، ومعاوية بن قرة: بإسكانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rūm means a Christian group. Adnā al-arḍ means the nearer land, relative to Mecca, the Persian realm, or Roman territory depending on the reported battle site; Imruʾ al-Qays's verse witnesses Adhriʿat's location.
rows.anchor: والروم: طائفة من النصارى، وأدنى الأرض: أقربهما

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi reads fī adnā al-arḍ; the interpretation of bidʿ depends on whether ghulibat is passive, or active with the Muslims defeating Persia at the term's limit.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكلبي: في أدنى الأرض، وتقدم الكلام في مدلول البضع باعتبار القراءتين

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr relates that Abu al-Hakam ibn Barjan derived the date and day of Jerusalem's conquest by Muslims from the opening verses, which occurred as predicted after Ibn Barjan's death; Abu Jaʿfar believed Ibn Barjan could extract hidden knowledge from scripture.
rows.anchor: كان شيخنا الأستاذ أبو جعفر بن الزبير يحكي عن أبي الحكم بن برجان أنه استخرج من قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command means His execution of judgments and direction of events as He wills.
rows.anchor: لله الأمر: أي إنفاذ الأحكام وتصريفها على ما يريد

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce min qablu wa-min baʿdu with both words built on ḍamma because their genitive complements are understood but omitted.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: من قبل ومن بعد، بضمهما: أي من قبل غلبة الروم ومن بعدها

rows.speaker: أبو السماك والجحدري وعون العقيلي
rows.claim: They read both adverbials with kasra and tanwin; al-Zamakhshari treats them as independent adverbs meaning earlier and later, while Ibn Atiyya reports a dialectal form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السماك، والجحدري، وعون العقيلي: من قبل ومن بعد، بالكسر والتنوين فيهما

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ allows dropping tanwin while retaining the form as though in annexation; al-Nahhas rejects this and says the forms are indefinite, meaning from an earlier or later time.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: ويجوز ترك التنوين، فيبقى كما هو في الإضافة

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi reports a Banu Asad usage with the first word genitive and tanwin, and the second in ḍamma without tanwin.
rows.anchor: وحكى الكسائي عن بعض بني أسد: لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm idhin is apparently an adverb modifying the believers' rejoicing; another parsing coordinates it with before and after to encompass past, future, and present before a new sentence.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن يومئذ ظرف يفرح المؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers rejoice at God's victory either of Rome over Persia, of Muslims over their enemies, the confirmation of the Prophet's prediction, or oppressors destroying one another.
rows.anchor: وبنصر الله: أي الروم على فارس، أو المسلمين على عدوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says Persia will have only one or two clashes, then no Persia, whereas Rome has successive generations until the end of time.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث: «فارس نطحة أو نطحتان، ثم لا فارس بعدها أبدا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Abu Saʿid say Badr defeated both idol-worshippers and fire-worshippers; another report links Muslim joy to Khosrow's death on the day of Hudaybiyya.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يوم بدر كانت هزيمة عبدة الأوثان وعبدة النيران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAziz describes God's vengeance on enemies and al-Rahim His mercy to allies.
rows.anchor: وهو العزيز بانتقامه من أعدائه، الرحيم لأوليائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waʿda Allāh is an accusative emphatic verbal noun reaffirming the preceding propositions that Rome will prevail and believers will rejoice.
rows.anchor: وانتصب وعد الله على أنه مصدر مؤكد لمضمون الجملة التي تقدمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people means Quraysh and others, ignorant of what benefits them in the afterlife though they know worldly states; one gloss says they fail to know events come from God and His promise and Messenger's report are true.
rows.anchor: ولكن أكثر الناس الكفار من قريش وغيرهم، لا يعلمون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والجمهور
rows.claim: They interpret knowledge of the world's outward aspect as expertise in visible worldly achievements: crafts, buildings, sources of wealth, and agriculture.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، والحسن، والجمهور: معناه ما فيه الظهور والعلو في الدنيا

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group understands the outward as transient worldly affairs with no lasting outcome; a Huthayli poetic phrase uses ẓāhir for something that has passed away.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: معناه ذاهبا زائلا، أي يعلمون أمور الدنيا التي لا بقاء لها

rows.speaker: ابن جبير والرماني
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says they know what soothsayers get from eavesdropping devils; al-Rummani says immediate sensory knowledge is outward, while rational inference is inward.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: ظاهرا، أي يعلمون من قبل الكهنة مما يسترقه الشياطين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari parses yaʿlamūn as replacing lā yaʿlamūn, equating ignorance with knowledge limited to worldly life; the world's deeper reality is a passage to the afterlife through obedience.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: يعلمون بدل من قول: لا يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating hum either emphasizes the pronoun or begins a new clause; either way, it highlights their heedlessness.
rows.anchor: وهم الثانية توكيد لهم الأولى، أو مبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase fī anfusihim can mean reflecting on their own creation, bringing them out of heedlessness to infer their creator.
rows.anchor: وفي أنفسهم: معمول ليتفكروا، إما على تقدير مضاف، أي في خلق أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing makes fī anfusihim the setting in which they reflect on the creation of the heavens and earth; it can also emphasize reflection, since thought occurs in the self.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر عقب هذا بأن الحق هو السبب في خلق السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the phrase depicts them generating reflection in their empty hearts, a vivid formulation since thought already occurs there.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: في هذا الوجه كأنه قال: أو لم يحدثوا التفكر في أنفسهم؟

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also connects fī to the verb reflect and treats what God created as the content of an implied statement; another view makes it mean that they might know this, inferred from the wording.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا: يكون صلة المتفكر، كقولك: تفكر في الأمر وأجال فكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative links the reflection directly to the following clause, with fī meaning bi; the author also allows tafakkarū to take the whole clause as its complement.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أولم يتفكروا متصل بما بعده، ومثله: ثم يتفكروا ما بصاحبهم من جنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase in themselves is emphatic because reflection occurs in the mind, just as writing occurs by hand.
rows.anchor: وفي أنفسهم: ظرف على سبيل التأكيد، لأن الفكر لا يكون إلا في النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Created in truth means the heavens and earth are inseparably joined to truth; the appointed term is the Hour, judgment, reward, and punishment, and meeting the Lord points to that end.
rows.anchor: وبالحق: في موضع الحال، أي وهي ملتبسة بالحق مقترنة به، وبتقدير أجل مسمى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says creation in truth serves rightful benefits: knowledge of God, worship, admonition, and mutual aid; the appointed term is Resurrection, signaling the world's end and the denial of meeting God.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: إلا بالحق، أي بسبب المنافع التي هي حق واجب

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi explains the ordering of proofs: a speaker begins with whichever evidence seems clearest and moves to the subtler, while a listener begins with the clearest; this explains self-first here and horizons-first in 41:53.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: قدم هنا دلائل الأنفس على دلائل الآفاق، وفي: سنريهم آياتنا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says many rather than most people reject the message after the clear proofs because some have accepted; the author says the explanation only works under a particular parsing and is compressed.
rows.anchor: وقال أيضا هنا: وإن كثيرا، وقبل، ولكن أكثر الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about traveling the earth is a reproachful assertion that they did travel and observe the fate of earlier deniers, who were stronger, plowed more land, and built more.
rows.anchor: أولم يسيروا في الأرض: هذا تقرير توبيخ، أي قد ساروا ونظروا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains athārū al-arḍ as plowing it.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: وأثاروا الأرض: حرثوها

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says they turned the land over for farming; other grammarians explain turning it for water, minerals, and sowing, since athāra is to stir something until dust rises.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: قلبوها للزراعة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن مجاهد وأبو الفتح وأبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads a lengthened form, which Ibn Mujahid rejects; Abu al-Fath calls it poetic metrical lengthening, not suitable to Quran, while Abu Haywa reads from athara (appropriation); another reading means they left traces.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: وآثاروا الأرض، بمدة بعد الهمزة. وقال ابن مجاهد: ليس بشيء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads their greater building and cultivation as sarcasm at Meccans, whose valley is barren and whose own strength and worldly status are meager.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أكثر مما عمروها: من عمارة أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about the worst end has several parses: the earlier readings raise ʿāqibatun and make al-sūʾā its predicate, with an kadhdhabū giving the cause; al-sūʾā may also be a verbal noun or an object of asāʾū.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحرميان، وأبو عمرو: ثم كان عاقبة بالرفع اسما لكان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers an explanatory-an parse and an appositional parse with an omitted predicate; the author calls the explanatory reading highly strained and the omitted predicate unsupported and ungrammatical by their school's rule.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يكون أن بمعنى: أي تفسير الإساءة التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The manuscript's unusual plural khaṭāyāt is not a productive form and is probably a copyist's added tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وأما قول الخطايات فكذا هو في النسخة التي طالعناها، جمع جمع تكسير بالألف والتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abd Allah and Talha read yubdiʾ with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on dāl; most read the latter open.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله وطلحة: يبدىء، بضم الياء وكسر الدال والجمهور: بفتحها

rows.speaker: الأبوان والجمهور
rows.claim: The two readers use third-person yarjiʿūn, while most address the audience as tarjiʿūn, meaning return to God's reward or punishment.
rows.anchor: والأبوان: يرجعون، بياء الغيبة والجمهور: بتاء الخطاب، أي إلى ثوابه وعقابه

rows.speaker: الجمهور وعلي والسلمي
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce yublisu with kasra on lām; Ali and al-Sulami open it, from a verb meaning to silence or dismay.
rows.anchor: والجمهور: يبلس، بكسر اللام وعلي والسلمي: بفتحها، من أبلسه إذا أسكته

rows.speaker: الجمهور وخارجة والأريس وابن سنان والأنطاكي
rows.claim: Most read lam yakun with masculine agreement; several transmitters read feminine takun.
rows.anchor: والجمهور: ولم يكن، بالياء وخارجة والأريس، كلاهما عن نافع، وابن سنان عن أبي جعفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partners are the idols worshippers served and associated with their wealth, or gods they claimed were God's partners; Muqatil instead says the supposed intercessors were angels, as in 39:3.
rows.anchor: من شركائهم: من الذين عبدوهم من دون الله، وهي الأوثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense kānū describes what will be their state when they see God's command, expressing certainty; the tanwin of yawmidhin replaces the omitted clause that the Hour occurs and criminals are stunned.
rows.anchor: وكانوا معناه: ويكون عند معاينتهم أمر الله وفساد حال الأصنام عبر بالماضي

rows.speaker: قتادة والزمخشري
rows.claim: Yatafarraqūn refers to believers and unbelievers, signaled by the next clauses; Qatada says it is an irreversible division, while al-Zamakhshari links it to the preceding return of creation.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: هي فرقة، لا اجتماع بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rawḍa means a land rich in plants and water, admired in Arab proverbs and poetry; yuhbarūn means they rejoice, with happiness visible on their faces.
rows.anchor: في روضة، الروضة، الأرض ذات النبات والماء

rows.speaker: الكسائي وعلي بن سليمان
rows.claim: Al-Kisaʾi glosses ḥabara as honoring and making comfortable; Ali ibn Sulayman associates it with visible traces of blessing.
rows.anchor: وحكى الكسائي: حبرته: أكرمته ونعمته. وقال علي بن سليمان:

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other lexical proposals derive the word from beautification or from elegant appearance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من التحبير، وهو التحسين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, and Mujahid say the believers will be honored.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، والضحاك، ومجاهد: يكرمون

rows.speaker: يحيى بن أبي كثير والأوزاعي ووكيع
rows.claim: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, al-Awzaʿi, and Wakiʿ say they will hear songs.
rows.anchor: وقال يحيى بن أبي كثير، والأوزاعي، ووكيع: يسمعون الأغاني

rows.speaker: أبو بكر وابن عباس وابن كيسان
rows.claim: Abu Bakr and Ibn Abbas say they will be crowned; Ibn Kaysan says they will be adorned.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر، وابن عباس: يتوجون على رؤوسهم. وقال ابن كيسان: يحلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥḍarūn means gathered for the punishment so none can be absent, as the Quran says they will not leave it.
rows.anchor: ومعنى محضرون: مجموعون له، لا يغيب أحد منهم عنه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the indefinite garden magnifies its unspecified quality; the present verb suggests recurring delights, while the active participle describes the unbelievers' fixed presence in punishment.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: والتنكير لإبهام أمرها وتفخيمه، وجاء يحبرون بالفعل المضارع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing creation's beginning and end in Paradise or Hell, God commands glorification; the apparent sense is glorification at these times for renewed blessings, or continual remembrance throughout one's life.
rows.anchor: لما بين تعالى عظيم قدرته في خلق السموات والأرض بالحق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the promise and warning are followed by mention of the deeds that lead to reward and rescue from punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: لما ذكر الوعد والوعيد، أتبعه ذكر ما يوصل إلى الوعد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: They interpret tasbih as prayer, assigning evening to Maghrib, morning to Fajr, and the other named times to Asr and Zuhr; ʿIsha is in the verse about nightfall.
rows.anchor: فعن ابن عباس وقتادة: المغرب والصبح والعصر والظهر، وأما العشاء ففي قوله: وزلفا من الليل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies the five prayers here and takes حين تمسون to include both Maghrib and ʿIsha.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: الخمس، وجعل حين تمسون شاملا للمغرب والعشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praise of God in the heavens and earth is parenthetical, affirming the duty of their inhabitants to praise Him.
rows.anchor: وله الحمد في السماوات والأرض: اعتراض بين الوقتين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan regards this verse as Medinan because, in his view, the five daily prayers were prescribed in Medina; most say they were prescribed in Mecca and included here.
rows.anchor: وكان الحسن يذهب إلى أن هذه الآية مدنية، لأنه كان يقول: فرضت الخمس بالمدينة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the five prayers are mentioned only in this passage.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: ما ذكرت الخمس إلا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Evening precedes morning as night precedes day; evening pairs with nightfall and morning with appearing in daylight, each followed by its opposite. Since no verb derives from ʿashī, the noun appears.
rows.anchor: وقدم الإمساء على الإصباح، كما قدم

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reads ḥīnan tam­sūna and ḥīnan tuṣbiḥūn with tanwin, treating the clauses as adjectives whose relative pronoun is omitted.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة: حينا تمسون وحينا تصبحون، بتنوين حين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of bringing the living from the dead and resurrection naturally follows the beginning and return of creation; likewise, people will emerge at the call as surely as creation began.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر الإبداء والإعادة، ناسب ذكره: يخرج الحي من الميت

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب وطلحة والأعمش
rows.claim: They read takhrujūn with an open tāʾ and ḍamma on rāʾ; most read the passive form with ḍamma on tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: تخرجون، بالتاء المضمومة، مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs progress from first human creation to resurrection: humans descend from Adam, whose origin was soil, and spread into worldly pursuits after a long interval.
rows.anchor: ومن آياته أن خلقكم من تراب: جعل خلقهم من تراب، حيث كان خلق أباهم آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating life from soil is a striking sign because dry, cold soil is furthest from living nature, which is warm and moist; the spirit is light and moving while soil is heavy and still.
rows.anchor: ونبه تعالى على عظيم قدرته بخلق الإنسان من تراب، وهو أبعد الأشياء عن درجة الإحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min anfusikum may mean Eve created from Adam's rib, as in 4:1, or spouses made of the same kind; shared nature creates affection and explains why messengers are human.
rows.anchor: من أنفسكم: فيها قولا وخلق منها زوجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sakan ilaihi means to incline toward someone; sakan is a noun in the passive sense.
rows.anchor: ويقال: سكن إليه: مال، ومنه السكن: فعل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وعكرمة
rows.claim: They take affection as sexual union and compassion as children, using the qualities as metonyms for spouses and offspring.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد والحسن وعكرمة: المودة: النكاح، والرحمة: الولد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other interpretations assign affection to a young wife and mercy to an old wife, a grown person and child, kinship ties, or affection from God and hatred from Satan.
rows.anchor: وقيل: مودة للشابة، ورحمة للعجوز. وقيل: مودة للكبير، ورحمة للصغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Different tongues are languages whose varied structures and rules are wondrous despite shared meanings; another view takes tongues as vocal sounds and tones.
rows.anchor: واختلاف ألسنتكم: أي لغاتكم، فمن اطلع على لغات رأى من اختلاف تراكيبها

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says the languages number seventy-two: seventeen among Ham's descendants, nineteen among Shem's, and thirty-six among Japheth's.
rows.anchor: وعن وهب: أن الألسنة اثنان وسبعون لسانا، في ولد حام سبعة عشر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari unusually interprets al-sina as palates, kinds and forms of seminal fluid, and the many distinctive qualities of every person's speech.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: الألسنة: اللذات وأجناس النطف وأشكاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Differences in color and bodily appearance enable recognition and transactions; myriad forms from one origin are a clear sign, and the verse is read with either open lām for the world or kasra for learned beneficiaries.
rows.anchor: وألوانكم: السواد والبياض وغيرهما، والأنواع والضروب بتخطيط الصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase by night and day most naturally modifies sleep, a favor especially relevant to those occupied at night; people may seek livelihood in either period.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن بالليل والنهار متعلق ب منامكم، فامتن تعالى بذلك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the paired phrases as a rhetorical wrap: sleep and work map to both times, or each may occur in both; the first reading best matches Quranic usage.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: هذا من باب اللف، وترتيبه: ومن آياته منامكم بالليل والنهار

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya rejects the reported word-order inversion: it is merely meant to pair sleep at night with livelihood by day, which the actual wording does not state.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وقال بعض المفسرين: في الكلام تقديم وتأخير، وهذا ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For showing lightning, min āyātihi may govern yurīkum directly, or the verb may imply an omitted an, or function as a verbal noun; these parses make the sign a nominal subject.
rows.anchor: ومن آياته يريكم البرق خوفا: إما أن يتعلق من آياته بيريكم

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani proposes an omitted bihā after the phrase, a grammatical analysis continued in the following discussion.
rows.anchor: وقال الرماني: يحتمل أن يكون التقدير:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Continuing al-Rummani interpretation from the preceding segment, the construction supplies bihā after the phrase; poetry supports the ellipsis.
rows.anchor: ومن آياته يريكم البرق بها، وحذف لدلالة من عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawfan and ṭamaʿan can be circumstantial verbal nouns or purposes; making them purposes needs an implied intention because the subject of yurīkum differs from the experiencers.
rows.anchor: وانتصب خوفا وطمعا على أنهما مصدران في موضع الحال، أي خائفين وطامعين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the people shown the lightning act as agents in meaning because they themselves see it; the author notes the grammatical dispute over whether an object of causative hamza retains agency.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: المفعولون فاعلون في المعنى، لأنهم راؤون مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A permissible alternative under the majority's shared-subject rule supplies the omitted phrase: God shows the lightning and they see it with fear and hope.
rows.anchor: ولو قيل: على مذهب من يشترطه. أن التقدير: يريكم البرق فترونه خوفا وطمعا

rows.speaker: الضحاك وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says fear is of lightning strikes and hope of rain; Qatada says travelers fear it while residents hope for rain.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: خوفا من صواعقه، وطمعا في مطره. وقال قتادة: خوفا للمسافر

rows.speaker: قيل وابن سلام
rows.claim: Other explanations say people fear false lightning or crop-destroying cold and hope for rain; a cited poem warns against lightning unaccompanied by rain.
rows.anchor: وقيل: خوفا أن يكون خلبا، وطمعا أن يكون ماطرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That the heavens and earth stand means they continue in place by God's command, as in the verse where people stand still in darkness.
rows.anchor: ومن آياته أن تقوم: أن تثبت وتمسك، مثل: وإذا أظلم عليهم قاموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first idhā is conditional and the second marks sudden response: resurrection follows one summons immediately, as a compliant hearer answers a caller.
rows.anchor: وإذا الأولى للشرط، والثانية للمفاجأة جواب الشرط، والمعنى: أنه لا يتأخر طرفة عين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min al-arḍ is linked to God's summons and daʿwatan means once, with no repeated call required; another view attaches min al-arḍ to daʿwatan.
rows.anchor: والدعوة: البعث من القبور، ومن الأرض يتعلق بدعاكم، ودعوة: أي مرة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says min marks the endpoint or source, as in calling someone who is on a mountain; the author rejects this grammar.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ومن عندي هنا لانتهاء الغاية، كما يقول: دعوتك من الجبل

rows.speaker: نافع ويعقوب
rows.claim: They pause after daʿwatan and restart at min al-arḍ; the author rejects this because it breaks the conditional from its response and improperly makes the sudden-response clause govern backward.
rows.anchor: وعن نافع ويعقوب: أنهما وقفا على دعوة، وابتدآ من الأرض

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari treats the conditional clause as a verbal noun equivalent to the sign of the heavens and earth standing, followed by the dead emerging at one command.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وقوله: إذا دعاكم بمنزلة قوله: يريكم في إيقاع الجملة موقع المفرد

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read takhrujūn with an open tāʾ and ḍamma on rāʾ; the rest of the canonical readers use passive tukhrajūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي: تخرجون، بفتح التاء وضم الراء وباقي السبعة: بضمها وفتح الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are ordered from the first creation of humans out of soil, to their spreading, then the creation of spouses from their own kind and affection between strangers; that last sign invites thought.
rows.anchor: وبدأ أولا من الآيات بالنشأة الأولى، وهي خلق الإنسان من التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence moves to visible signs for all: heavens, earth, languages, and colors, which are enduring human traits.
rows.anchor: ثم أتبعه بما هو مشاهد للعالم كلهم، وهو خلق السموات والأرض، واختلاف اللغات والألوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sleep and pursuit of livelihood are intermittent rather than constant; calling the audience to hear reminds them that worship may require guidance.
rows.anchor: ثم أتبعه بالمنام والابتغاء، وهما من الأمور المفارقة في بعض الأوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lightning precedes rain like a herald, and both atmospheric signs precede the earthly revival; their varied occurrence by place, time, and intensity points to a free agent rather than routine nature.
rows.anchor: وقدمها على ما هو من الأرض، وهو الإتيان والإحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The list ends with the constant standing of heaven and earth, which is astonishing without supports, then returns to resurrection; each domain is illustrated by paired permanent and intermittent signs.
rows.anchor: ثم ختم هذه الآيات بقيام السموات الأرض، وذلك من العوارض اللازمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All in the heavens and earth belong to God and are subject to His dominion and coercive power.
rows.anchor: من في السماوات والأرض: عام في كونهم تحت ملكه وقهره

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says qānitūn means standing as witnesses to God's unity, as the cited couplet says every thing bears a sign of His oneness.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: قانتون: قائمون بالشهادة على وحدانيته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains qānitūn as compliant with God's administration: none can resist His will for life, death, health, or illness; this is obedience to will, not worship.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: مطيعون، أي في تصريفه، لا يمتنع عنه شيء يريد فعله بهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they will stand on the Resurrection Day; other proposals take qānitūn as sincerity or acknowledgment of servitude, or distinguish between believers and unbelievers under a general wording.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قائمون يوم القيامة، يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym take ahwan to mean easy rather than comparative, since the two acts do not differ in difficulty for God; the wording also appears in Ibn Masud codex.
rows.anchor: وكذا هو في مصحف عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A comparative reading measures by human observation: restoring many things is easier than beginning them, though both acts are equally effortless for God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أهون للتفضيل، وذلك بحسب معتقد البشر وما يعطيهم النظر في المشاهد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading refers the pronoun to creation: return is easier and faster for creatures because first creation proceeds through stages while resurrection requires only a command.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الضمير في عليه عائد على الخلق، أي والعود أهون على الخلق
